draft.title: Jewish sexual ethics
card: Jewish teaching sees sexuality as a good gift from God. It is valued most within marriage, where it expresses commitment and can lead to children.

Many of the rules come from the Torah and are developed by rabbis in the Talmud and later law. Traditional teaching includes the laws of family purity (niddah), which set times of separation between a married couple each month.
holds that the halakhah (Jewish law) is binding and keeps traditional rules. It teaches that sexual relations belong within marriage between a man and a woman.
Reform and Liberal movements treat the tradition as open to reinterpretation. They apply its values in new ways, such as accepting same-sex couples, and many do not follow niddah as binding law.
draft.remember: Judaism values sexuality within marriage, but the movements differ in how they apply the rules.

a.q: Which statement best describes Jewish teaching on sexuality?
opts: It is a good gift, valued most within marriage
It is a necessary evil, tolerated only for having children
It is a private matter with no guidance from Jewish law
It is a good gift, equally valued in any relationship
a.why: Judaism sees sexuality as good and gives it its fullest place in marriage, where it expresses commitment. The view that it is only tolerated is tempting, but the card says it is a gift and not an evil.
a.clue: Think about where the card says sexuality is valued most.

b.q: Two Jewish couples in Sydney, one Orthodox and one Reform, ask their rabbis about observing niddah. Why might the answers differ?
opts: The movements differ on whether halakhah binds today
Only Orthodox Jews accept the Torah as a holy text
Reform Judaism rejects marriage as a Jewish value
Orthodox rabbis hold that niddah is only a custom
b.why: Orthodox Judaism treats halakhah as binding, so niddah is kept as law. Progressive movements reinterpret the tradition and many do not treat it as binding. The idea that Reform rejects marriage is wrong, because the movements share the value of marriage and differ in how they apply the rules.
b.clue: The difference lies in how each movement treats Jewish law.

a.best: It is a good gift, valued most within marriage

b.best: The movements differ on whether halakhah binds today
